cards.title: Unified Information-Theoretic Identifiability Criterion
cards.claim: Identifiability can be assessed by analyzing the relationship between the determinant of the Fisher Information Matrix (|MF|) and the residual noise variance (σ²). For structurally identifiable fixed-effects models, log|MF| shows a continuous linear relationship with log(σ²) and approaches infinity as σ² approaches zero. For mixed-effects models, the relationship is continuous but asymptotes to a constant value rather than infinity.
conditions: Applicable to both fixed-effects and mixed-effects (population) PK/PD models.
Requires computation of the Jacobian matrix and the Fisher Information Matrix.
Assumes equal variances across observation points (though this can be relaxed).
required_inputs: Structural model equations (fixed and random effects).
Parameter vector (Θ) and variance-covariance matrix of random effects (Ω).
limitations: A full-rank local information matrix does not guarantee global identifiability.
The method is model- and design-specific.
Does not explicitly assess deterministic identifiability directly, but allows inference via Cramér-Rao bounds on parameter precision.
cards.downstream_use: Use this method to screen for local/design-dependent identifiability issues in proposed PK/PD model structures before data collection or model fitting. It helps identify parameters that may be unidentifiable under specific designs, requiring fixing or re-parameterization.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
